subject: GreenPoint: data use, no-train opt-out and subprocessors
messages:
From: Evelyn Shaw <evelyn.shaw@greenpoint.ai>

Cc: GreenPoint Legal <legal@greenpoint.ai>, Marco Rojas <mrojas@procure.greenpoint.ai>

Subject: Initial questions — data use & model improvement opt-out

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — GreenPoint liked the latency profile and observability. Before we proceed to procurement, Legal wants to clarify how Redwood treats customer prompts/responses and whether we can get a firm "no-training" or "no-model-improvement" commitment for our workspace. A few specific asks from our side: 

- Can you confirm that prompts/responses submitted to the hosted API are segregated per account and not used to train Redwood models by default?
- Do you offer a contractual opt-out for model improvement (i.e., we would explicitly prohibit Redwood from using our data to improve models or internal training corpora)? If so, is that an add-on or included in the enterprise DPA?
- What subprocessors do you use for telemetry, logging, and model hosting (we are particularly concerned about third-party model inference providers and metrics ingestion)?
- Cross-border transfer: we have EU customers and want to understand whether any data is processed outside the US and what safeguards are in place (SCCs, encryption-at-rest, customer-managed keys).

Attached is GreenPoint's standard DPA questionnaire — Legal would appreciate a point-by-point response or a redline of your DPA.

Can we schedule a short call with someone from your privacy/security team this week? Marco is coordinating procurement.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Shaw
Head of Data Governance
GreenPoint Analytics

Subject: Re: Initial questions — data use & model improvement opt-out

Evelyn, thanks — glad GreenPoint is evaluating Redwood. I've put answers inline and attached our latest DPA draft for review (Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf). High-level summary up front: we offer an explicit contractual "no-training/no-model-improvement" option as part of our enterprise DPA (no extra charge). Details below.

1) Segregation and default behavior
- By default (hosted API), we isolate customer workspaces and store prompt/response logs for a limited retention window to support billing, troubleshooting, and abuse detection. Default settings do not automatically feed customer data into Redwood's internal model training corpus.

2) Contractual opt-out for model improvement
- Option A (No-Train): Redwood will not use any Customer Data (prompts, responses, embeddings, or derived artifacts) to train, fine-tune, or evaluate models for the purpose of model improvement. This is a contractual commitment we can add to Section 6 of the DPA.
- Option B (Metadata-only learning): for customers who opt-in, we may collect high-level telemetry (latency, error rates) in aggregated, non-identifying form — never prompt/response text.

3) Prompt/response ownership and export
- Customers retain ownership of their prompts and generated outputs. We can add an explicit clause that grants the customer perpetual export rights and a copy-on-request process for data export within 30 days of request.

4) Subprocessors
- Primary subprocessors: cloud provider (GCP/US-west), observability vendor (LogStream Inc.), metrics ingestion (TelemetryCo). For hosted inference we run models in our managed fleet; we do not pass raw prompt/response text to third-party model vendors without a customer opt-in. Full subprocessors list is in Appendix B of the attached DPA and we commit to 30-day notice for material changes.

5) Cross-border transfer and keys
- For customers requiring EU residency: we offer EU-hosted tenancy. We also support customer-managed keys (KMS) and will include SCCs where applicable. On-prem/private deployments are also available as an option.

Next steps:
- I've attached Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf with the proposed "No-Train" clause in Section 6. Monica (our Privacy Lead) is on cc and will propose specific redline language to make it operational (data scopes, retention limits, auditability).
- If that looks good, Marco — can we get your procurement slot for a DocuSign run and target SLA questions?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

Subject: Fwd: Redlines — suggested DPA language for no-train and data export

Evelyn/Marco — forwarding with redlined language and a few operational notes. High-level comments: make the "No-Train" clause explicit and operationalize it with definitions and audit rights. I've included suggested clause text below; feel free to pull into your DPA.

-- Suggested clause excerpts (for insertion into Section 6):
"No-Training Commitment": Redwood will not use Customer Data (defined as prompts, responses, embeddings, logs, or other content submitted by Customer or its End Users) for the purpose of training, improving, or evaluating models that are used to provide services to any third party, except as may be required by law. This commitment includes derived features and embeddings.

"Data Export and Retention": Customer may request a full export of Customer Data. Redwood will provide the export within 30 days in a machine-readable format. Default retention for prompt/response logs is 30 days for hosted customers; customers may shorten or disable retention as part of the No-Train option.

"Audit and Verification": Upon reasonable notice, Redwood will allow an independent, mutually agreed auditor to verify compliance with the No-Training Commitment. Audit scope will be limited to data handling practices and will exclude access to proprietary model internals.

Operational notes:
- Logging/metrics: for troubleshooting we keep temporary telemetry; we will redact prompt text from any logs forwarded to third-party vendors.
- Subprocessors: any subprocessors that handle prompt/response data will be contractually bound to the same No-Training terms.
- KMS/SCCs: recommend GreenPoint chooses EU-hosted tenancy or customer-managed KMS if residency is a hard requirement.

If you want, we can produce a short one-page attestation for procurement that summarizes the commitments for signature.

Monica Patel
Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Monica/Karthik — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the draft language. A few clarifying points from Legal and Procurement: 

- Audit: GreenPoint is comfortable with an independent auditor approach provided we can validate the scope includes verification of data flows to subprocessors and any redaction process for logs.
- Retention: 30 days default is acceptable. For production EU customers we'll request EU tenancy; confirm that the export process supports PII-preserving deltas (we only need user-level outputs, not raw logs).
- Subprocessors: please send the full current list and confirm you will add contractual parity for the No-Train clause (i.e., subprocessors that handle Customer Data are contractually prohibited from using it for model improvement).

Procurement asked about timing for final DPA and DocuSign: can you target a signed DPA by 2026-02-12 so we can begin a Q1 trial? We'll also need a short attestation for our security questionnaire to close the loop.

Appreciate it — will await the finalized redline and subprocessors list.

Best,
Evelyn
